messages:
cheng: bringing up astrax-lite-7b-int4 on dedicated pool, seeing a small but consistent drift vs fp16 on our summarization evals. outputs are fluent but drop a key entity ~30% of the time on long contexts. suspecting a rotary phase / kv-cache handshake mismatch after conversion + tokenizer normalization oddities. anyone run into diacritic-token shifts with these conversions?

maria: yup, seen something similar on OrpheusX. usually ends up being a tokenizer normalizer (NFC vs NFKC) + an off-by-one in how we map token ids into rotary positions during export.

sam: can you paste a minimal repro of the mismatch? short examples help. also which quant pipeline did you use (our q4/q2 or the custom int4 script)?

cheng: quick repro below — this is from the eval harness with longctx=2048.
```text
input: "Résumé — meeting notes: Discuss budget for Q3; attendees: José, Zoë, Søren."
fp16_summary: "Budget for Q3 discussed, attendees José, Zoë, Søren. Action: follow-up on line items."
int4_summary: "Budget for Q3 discussed, attendees Zoė, Soren. Action: follow-up."  # dropped José and diacritics changed order
```
we used our int4 pipeline (block-quantize + symmetric rounding) with the headwise kernel enabled.

eli: this smells like tokenization normalization + token-id -> rotary-index mapping. first triage: run token id sequences for the examples under the converter we used and under HF tokenizer with NFKC. compare lengths and any inserted sentinel tokens.

ciara: also check that kv cache indexing isn't shifting when compressing keys for int4 kernels. some kernels pack heads differently and if we accidentally use a per-head offset from the fp16 runtime you get a phase handshake mismatch.

sam: two quick tests to isolate: 1) re-run tokenizer with NFKC and compare token ids for the sentence; 2) run the model with fp16 weights but force the int4 runtime path (no quantized weights) to see if kernel packing alone changes behavior.

maria: I'll run the tokenizer NFKC vs NFC diff and post token id sequences. giving me 30m.

cheng: thanks. i'll dump the converter args: `--export-format rw-fused --rotary-mode headdim-offset --norm none` — we previously exported with `norm none` because we assumed upstream tokenizers already normalized. maybe that's a bad assumption.

rotary-checker-bot: lint results: export used `rotary: headdim-offset` and headcount OK, but detected uneven headpacking for int4 kernel variant v2. recommend running `rw-check-rotary --compat` before deploy.

eli: good catch bot. ciara, can you verify the int4 kernel packaging flags? if packaging changed between v1->v2 that would explain a deterministic phase shift.

ciara: looking now — int4 v2 packs heads into groups of 3 for better cache locality, while fp16 and int4-v1 used group-of-4. that re-pairing will shift per-head rotary multipliers unless we remap indices during export.

sam: OK actionable plan:
- maria: tokenization normalization diff + token id dump (owner)
- cheng: re-export with `--rotary-map remap-per-head` and test (owner)
- ciara: add compatibility shim in int4 runtime to remap old head indices temporarily (owner)
- eli: queue eval rerun for summarization and our QA prompt suite once the above are in (owner)

maria: token id dump (NFC vs NFKC) -> pasted: `NFC: [502, 1203, 34, 9982, 77, 908]` `NFKC: [502, 1203, 34, 9982, 77, 908]` — weird both same for this example. but for some other names (José -> different codepoint sequences) NFKC reduces length by 1. attaching sample list in RW-1234.

cheng: filing RW ticket: <https://redwood-internal/issue/1234|RW-1234> with logs and the conversion args. I'll try re-export with remap and post results.

ciara: provisional hotfix: runtime shim added on a branch that detects pack pattern and remaps rotary indices -> will run unit tests. if green i'll push a canary.

sam: once canary is up, eli can run the eval harness. if we recover entity recall and reduce diacritic drops, we close. if not, fallback is keep fp16 for this model until we have a safer quant path.

eli: scheduling the eval job for when cheng/ciara push artifacts. tagging @maria for token list.

cheng: pushed a quick re-export with `--rotary-map remap-per-head` and attached weights to RW-1234. initial local run looks closer to fp16 (entity recall up ~12%). will confirm with full eval.

maria: token list for problematic samples attached to the ticket. looks like a minority of tokens cause the mismatch but they blow up on long contexts.

ciara: unit tests passed for remap shim. canary build `int4-v2-remap-202` ready at `s3://redwood-canaries/int4-v2-remap-202/`.

eli: kicked off evals against summarization and our regression suite. ETA ~45m.

sam: nice. thanks everyone. keep notes minimal in the ticket — include the kernel packing change, tokenizer differences, and the remediation steps.

cheng: will update RW-1234 with results when eval completes. leaning optimistic but leaving rolling fallback policy ready. :thumbsup:"
